expectations.text: Explains a VPN routes/sends the user's internet traffic through another computer/server first
expectations.evidence: Describes encryption ("wraps your data in a locked box") and location-masking clearly, but never explicitly states traffic passes through another server/computer first — the routing mechanism is implied, not stated

expectations.text: Explains this hides the user's real location and/or hides their browsing activity from their own ISP/network
expectations.evidence: "the website sees the VPN's location instead of yours"; "If you don't want your internet provider or advertisers tracking exactly what you do online, a VPN hides that from them"

expectations.text: Uses full grammatical sentences throughout, not sentence fragments
expectations.evidence: All five paragraphs are complete, connected sentences with explicit reasoning

expectations.text: Does not use technical jargon without immediately explaining it in plain words
expectations.evidence: "IP address, which is like your device's home address on the internet" — explained on first use

expectations.text: Does not include marketing language or brand promotion
expectations.evidence: Actively pushes back on hype: "The ads you keep seeing are companies competing for your attention because privacy sells well, not because everyone secretly needs one every day"
